title: The finite-origin evaluation has the common-stage internal-Hom universal property
statement: Under the same finite-field, prime, independent algebraic-closure universe, and separated finite-type scheme hypotheses as [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], let B be any Duality with its recorded finite-origin normalization. Every pair (op K,B.omega) is in commonStageHomPairs. There is a natural isomorphism from B.duality.dual to the actual common-stage internal Hom into B.omega, and for every K,P the map h to tensor.map(identity K,h) followed by B.evaluation K is a bijection. In other words the specified InternalHom B is nonempty.

source.place: Final coefficient-transport paragraph (thm-coef-qbar-verdier); formal expansion of retained proof step 5, tensor-Hom adjunction and actual internal Hom; detailed retained argument: dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/thm-coef-qbar-verdier.json, original proof steps

proof.text: For any two pairs choose their literal compositum. The finite HomIdentification at that field supplies precisely the permitted-pair predicate in commonStageHomPairs, proving that all these pairs are permitted. The finite evaluation transpose is the composite of postcomposition with HomIdentification.duality and the inverse of HomIdentification.adjunction.homEquiv. Its evaluation clause identifies this composite with the displayed tensor-evaluation formula; hence finite_evaluation_transpose_bijective is proved directly.

Put K,P and omega and a morphism at a common field. The finite evaluation-transpose bijection and its inverse commute with scalar extension by the finite Hom comparison and the recorded evaluation square. Hence both maps preserve eventual equality of representatives. Their composites are the identities at the representative field, so they induce inverse natural bijections of common-stage Hom sets.

The specified object and arrow formulas for commonStageDerivedInternalHom identify its functor with this right adjoint. Uniqueness of the right adjoint gives the natural isomorphism to the dual. The finite evaluation square identifies its actual evaluation transpose with h mapped by tensor then B.evaluation, giving the required universal property.
